facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
no history of liver disease
leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2)
Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts

concepts.why: The patient developed jaundice and elevated liver enzymes after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a drug-induced liver injury.
The patient has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia, which is supported by the prostate-specific antigen level and uroflowmetry results.
The patient has reduced urine flow and obstructive findings on uroflowmetry, suggesting a urinary obstruction.
The patient has elevated bilirubin levels and normal abdominal ultrasonography, suggesting a cholestatic pattern of liver injury.
The patient has elevated liver enzymes, suggesting a hepatocellular injury.
The patient developed liver injury after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a possible hepatotoxic effect of the medication.

rationales.F05: The patient's symptoms of loss of appetite, malaise, generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice suggest liver injury.
rationales.F09: The elevated AST level is a strong indicator of liver injury.
rationales.F10: The elevated ALT level is a strong indicator of liver injury.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient developed liver injury after starting Alfuzosin, with elevated AST and ALT levels, and the temporal relationship between Alfuzosin use and liver injury onset supports Alfuzosin-induced hepatotoxicity.
